definitions.explanation: The three-stroke radical ({氵|さんずい}) derived from {水|みず}, used in kanji related to water or liquids.

examples.japanese: さんずい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{水|みず}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{関係|かんけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ある。
examples.english: Kanji with the sanzui radical are related to water.

examples.japanese: さんずい⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{調|しら}べる→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧。
examples.english: To look it up by the sanzui radical.

notes:
さんずい is one of the most common kanji radicals. The name comes from {三|さん} (three) + {水|すい} (water), describing its three-stroke shape derived from {水|みず}.

KANJI WITH さんずい:
- {海|うみ} (sea), {池|いけ} (pond), {湖|みずうみ} (lake)
- {泳|およ}ぐ (to swim), {洗|あら}う (to wash)
- {波|なみ} (wave), {汗|あせ} (sweat), {涙|なみだ} (tears)
- {温|あたた}かい (warm), {深|ふか}い (deep)

USAGE:
Knowing radicals helps with kanji dictionary lookup and guessing meanings. Almost all kanji with さんずい relate to water, liquids, or fluidity.

RELATED RADICAL TERMS:
- {部首|ぶしゅ}: radical (general term)
- にんべん: person radical
- きへん: tree radical
- てへん: hand radical
- ごんべん: speech radical
